meta.title: cilento.eu — Where the Greeks built in stone, the sea answered in caves
meta.description: cilento.eu — 100 km of coastline between Poseidonia and Palinuro: Doric temples, sea caves, villages, National Park and Mediterranean Diet.

hero.kicker: National Park · UNESCO 1998 · 100 km of coastline
hero.title: Where the Greeks built in stone,
hero.lede: Doric temples Athens no longer has, bays that open only from the sea, villages where Ancel Keys understood why people live longer here. Tell me what kind of traveler you are — I'll tell you which Cilento is yours.

facts.dd: 2nd largest National Park in Italy — Law 394/91
Paestum, Velia, Certosa di Padula — whc 842

hero.routesLine: From abroad: London · Paris · Amsterdam · Barcelona · Madrid → Salerno QSR, 40′ from Paestum.

destinazioni.title: Destinations
destinazioni.sub: Each with its own sea, its own stone, its own rhythm. Filter by desire, not by stars.

items.title: Paestum — Poseidonia
items.desc: At 7am, among poppies and blond travertine, the three temples of the 6th–5th century BC buzz only with cicadas — Athens, this intact, no longer has them.
items.meta: 40.4239°N 15.0053°E · 1h from Salerno · half day + buffalo DOP

items.title: Palinuro, Aeneas's helmsman
items.desc: Natural Arch at the bow, then a dip at Buondormire where the sand crackles white and the cliff smells of warm resin.

items.title: Marina di Camerota
items.desc: From Lentiscelle to Cala Bianca you count the Saracen towers by swimming, with the oil of century-old olive trees still on your hands from lunch.
items.meta: Only on foot or by canoe · Marine Protected Area
items.alt: Mingardo Beach at Marina di Camerota

items.title: Acciaroli + Pioppi
items.desc: In the evening the harbor turns off its engines and only the clink of glasses remains — here Hemingway listened to fishermen and Keys measured longevity with EVO oil.
items.meta: Museum of the Mediterranean Diet · 5 Sails

items.title: Castellabate
items.desc: From the Norman castle descend toward Punta Licosa among crushed myrtle, and the Tyrrhenian below is bottle-green against white limestone.
items.meta: Marine Protected Area · Belvedere at sunset
items.alt: Santa Maria di Castellabate from the village

items.title: Velia — Elea
items.desc: Walk the Porta Rosa, the first full-span Greek arch, where Parmenide thought of being — below, ten minutes away, Ascea Marina puts your feet back in water.
items.meta: UNESCO · ideal with Paestum in one day

items.title: Agropoli
items.desc: Steep stone steps, Aragonese castle against the wind, and at Trentova the water tastes of real salt after the train from Naples — this is the gateway, not a stopover.
items.meta: Train station · base without rental car

items.title: Teggiano + Certosa di Padula
items.desc: At Pertosa you enter by boat into the dark that smells of cold river, at Padula you exit into 51,500 m² of Baroque — stone, cave water and wood-fired bread.
items.meta: Pertosa 16° constant · car, torch, fleece needed

items.title: Swim in the caves
items.desc: Palinuro and Camerota: boat trips at dawn, Blue Cave, Blood Cave, swim at Buondormire. Bring rock shoes.

items.title: Walk among the Greeks
items.desc: Paestum + Velia in one day with audioguide and museum. At Paestum on August 18–19 the columns align at sunset.

items.title: Climb into the Park
items.desc: Mount Cervati (1,898 m), Calore Gorges, Capelli di Venere waterfall, Castelcivita and Pertosa caves. On foot or by e-bike.
li: Torch and fleece even in August

items.title: Eat slowly
items.desc: Mozzarella in the same morning, Menaica anchovies, Felitto fusillo, white fig DOP, EVO oil. In Pioppi you understand why people live long.

primavera.title: Spring — empty excavations and broom
primavera.text: April-May: 18–22°, poppies among the temples, Monte Stella trails without heat. Paestum and Velia almost deserted in the morning. Artichoke and strawberry festivals.
primavera.meta: Sea: 17–19° · Ideal for: archaeology, trekking, cycling

estate.title: Summer — dawn by boat, siesta in shade
estate.text: June-August: Buondormire Bay and Cala Bianca before 10, villages after 9pm. Book boats and tables. Punta Licosa on foot at sunset, not at 1pm.
estate.meta: Sea: 24–27° · Ideal for: caves, kayak, fish festivals

autunno.title: Autumn — new oil and low light
autunno.text: September-October: the best month. Water still 23–25°, empty beaches, harvest and open oil mills. Teggiano and Padula with beautiful morning mists.
autunno.meta: Sea: 21–25° · Ideal for: food, trekking, temple photos

inverno.title: Winter — fireplaces and Certosa
inverno.text: November-March: real villages, no queues. Certosa di Padula, Pertosa Caves (always 16° inside), chickpea soup and lagane. Cervati sometimes snowy.
inverno.meta: Sea: 14–16° · Ideal for: inland, speleology, cuisine

itinerari.title: Three honest itineraries
itinerari.sub: Real driving times, no 'everything in one day'.

items.title: Essential Magna Graecia
steps: Naples → Paestum (museum + temples at sunset), night in Agropoli. Buffalo in Capaccio.
Velia in the morning + Ascea Marina in the afternoon. Evening in Acciaroli.
Pioppi (Mediterranean Diet) + Castellabate, return from Agropoli FS.

items.title: Wild coast by boat
steps: Base in Palinuro: caves by boat, Buondormire, Primula at sunset.
Marina di Camerota: Infreschi by kayak, Cala Bianca, evening in Pisciotta.
Scario + Blue Cave, dinner of Menaica anchovies.
items.meta: Book boat the day before · rock shoes

items.title: Complete Park
steps: Certosa di Padula + Capelli di Venere.
Cervati or Calore Gorges + Paestum finale.
items.meta: Car needed · inland roads slow, and beautiful

items.title: Mozzarella di Bufala DOP
items.desc: Dairies in Capaccio-Paestum — eat it within 6 hours, still warm.

items.title: Menaica Anchovies
items.desc: Pisciotta — caught with the net that selects, Slow Food presidium.

items.title: Felitto Fusillo + lagane e ceci
items.desc: Pasta drawn on a brass rod, mountain meat sauces.

items.title: White Fig of Cilento DOP + EVO Oil
Wine: Aglianico and Fiano del Cilento DOC
items.desc: Wineries between Rutino, Agropoli and San Mauro.

routes.title: By plane: Salerno QSR
routes.desc: The Costa d'Amalfi and Cilento Airport is in Pontecagnano, 40′ from Paestum. Direct flights from abroad (source: aeroportosalerno.it, Oct 2026 — seasonal routes change, check the airline's website):
routes.meta: From QSR: Airlink bus → Salerno station 30–40′ ~€5, then Regional to Agropoli–Ascea–Sapri. Alternative: Naples-Capodichino + Alibus.

treno.title: By train
treno.desc: Tyrrhenian line Naples–Reggio Calabria. The Regional Naples C.–Sapri (~2h45) stops at Paestum, Agropoli-Castellabate, Ascea, Pisciotta, Centola-Palinuro-Marina di Camerota, Policastro, Sapri — Naples→Agropoli ~1h35 (source: live RFI monitor).

list.route: Italo direct to Agropoli · from Naples ~1h, from Rome ~2h04
InterCity Night from Milan · arrives in Agropoli at dawn
Vallo di Diano · no train since 1987

treno.meta: Live times: RFI monitor and trenitalia.com — Sicignano-Lagonegro has never reopened.

auto.title: By car + when
auto.desc: A2: exits Battipaglia–Eboli for Paestum and Agropoli; Atena Lucana–Sala Consilina–Padula-Buonabitacolo for Teggiano, Padula and Pertosa; highway for Policastro and Sapri. SS18 coast road: Agropoli→Palinuro ~55 km in ~1h20, slow and beautiful — in summer parking is full before 10. Locally: summer Cilento Blu bus between villages, shared boat at Palinuro/Camerota from €25.
auto.meta: We don't book anything: times and prices change, check at the harbor, museum, station.
